reply.subject: RSW_Mynock

observed./mnt/d/ClaudeWork/rimmandrake/art_eval/r: The same picture three times at one scale. A creature shown from above with its wings spread flat. A thin, segmented tail points straight up and ends in a small pointed spade. Two broad, ragged, finger-ribbed wings stretch left and right, with claw-like points along the top edges. A short wrinkled body runs down to a head at the bottom of the frame. The head has two bulging dark eyes on knobs at the sides and a large round open mouth ringed with pale bristles, facing the viewer. The hide is mottled olive, tan and reddish with a wet, wrinkled texture. The background is transparent.

The same spread-winged picture, seen from above with the head at the bottom: bulging eyes and a bristled round sucker mouth toward the viewer, tail pointing up, wings flat out to the sides. Clean alpha.
Pixel for pixel the same picture as south: a symmetric spread-wing view with the face and sucker mouth visible. It is not a side profile.
Pixel for pixel the same picture as south. The eyes and the bristled sucker mouth are fully visible. No rear view.

Beside the vanilla human at max zoom the mynock is small, about half a cell across, roughly the size of the human's head. At 32 px per cell it is a tiny speckled cross shape that barely reads against the dirt floor.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face (eyes and sucker mouth), but as part of an overhead spread-wing view: the back, wings and an upward-pointing tail are seen from above. It is not a front view from the game camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North is the same file as south, so the bulging eyes and the bristled sucker mouth are fully visible on the rear facing.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: Every facing is the same dorsal plan view: wings laid flat to both sides, tail straight up the canvas, head at the bottom. That is a top-down layout, not the angled game camera.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Measured spread is 0% (218 px on every facing).

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: There is one picture for all facings, so nothing turns with the body. East shows a symmetric front/top view instead of a profile, with wings spread to both sides.

SIGNATURE.seen: The broad leathery wings, whip tail and bristled sucker mouth are all clearly visible.

ALIEN.seen: The bristled sucker mouth, eyes on knobs and mottled wet hide make it read as alien rather than as a bat.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1) Mottled, wrinkled mineral-like hide, no fur: present. 2) Round bristled sucker mouth, no snout: present. 3) Long thin segmented whip tail: present. 4) Broad leathery wings form most of the outline, no bat ears or bat face: present.

CANON.seen: Present: bat-like wings, sucker disc with bristles, eyes on knobs, a tail ending in a spade, ragged wing edges with wrist claws. Absent: the two small clawed hind legs are not visible. Colour layout: the body is mottled olive, tan and red, not clearly darker than the wings. The rendering is realistic, but the edge is a thin dark outline.

STYLE.seen: Realistic, wrinkled, wet-looking texture with natural shading. Not cute or cel-shaded. The eyes are glossy but bulging and alien, not cute.

OURS.seen: Provenance is a texPath under RimStarWars/SWBestiary, which is live installed art from another mod's art set, not art generated for this subject.

ALPHA.seen: Clean transparent background on every facing; no shadow or ground baked in.

SCALE.seen: Small next to the human, about head-sized, which fits 'a small parasite'.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it is a tiny speckled cross with low contrast against the dirt floor, so the shapes barely read.

WINGS_FOLDED.seen: The wings are fully spread and flat to both sides in the only picture, which is also the grounded picture.

request.subject: RSW_Mynock

edits.change: The north view is the rear view, seen from behind: the back of the small dark body, the folded wing backs along the sides and the whip tail hanging down, with the head tucked out of sight so no eyes and no sucker mouth show.
Each facing is drawn from the angled three-quarter game camera, a little above the creature, with the body upright and the wings folded close at the sides, never spread flat as a plan view.

The south view is the front view, eyes toward the viewer: the round bristled sucker mouth and bulging eyes face the camera, the chest and body sit below the head, the wings are folded along the sides and the whip tail hangs behind the body.

The east view is a true side profile: the head with the sucker disc points right, one folded wing is visible along the flank, two thin hind legs sit below the body and the whip tail trails to the left.
Three separate pictures are painted, one each for south (front), east (side profile) and north (rear), each with its own pose and visible surface, sharing one palette and one body plan.
The mynock is painted fresh in the painterly vanilla RimWorld style from the description alone, with reference: none, so no existing Star Wars bestiary art is the source.

Two small, thin, clawed hind legs show under the body. The body and head are the darkest dark olive-brown, and the wing membranes are slightly lighter and translucent. The edges carry a clean dark outline.

invariants: small silicon-based parasite body with a stony, mineral-textured hide instead of fur
round bristled sucker mouth in place of a mammal face, no bat ears or bat face
broad leathery wings that form most of the outline, folded at the sides in the south and north views
transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline
small creature that reads clearly at 0.6 tile draw size
request.prompt: A single RimWorld creature sprite sheet of a mynock, a small silicon-based vacuum parasite, in the painterly vanilla RimWorld style: realistic, hand-painted, clean dark outline, transparent background. Three separate pictures of the same creature, each from the angled game camera slightly above the creature, with the body upright. Body plan for all three: a small compact body with a stony, mineral-textured hide, the darkest dark olive-brown on the body and head; broad leathery wings that make up most of the outline, slightly lighter and translucent in the membranes, with visible veins; a round bristled sucker mouth in place of a face; two bulging eyes above the mouth; two small, thin, clawed hind legs under the body; a long, thin whip-like tail. No bat ears and no bat snout. Picture 1, front view, eyes toward the viewer: the round bristled sucker mouth and eyes face the camera, the chest and body sit below the head, the wings are folded along the sides and the whip tail hangs behind the body, the two hind legs visible under the body. Picture 2, side profile: the head with the sucker disc points right, one folded wing lies along the flank, the two thin hind legs sit below the body, and the whip tail trails to the left. Picture 3, rear view, seen from behind: the back of the dark body, the folded wing backs along the sides and the whip tail hanging down, the head tucked out of sight so only the back of the body shows, hind legs visible at the bottom. All three share the same palette, proportions and wing shape, and read clearly at a small size.
